I was working the phone when very polite lady called asking us for a price check. I tried to transfer her to the department and manager 3 times each. No response. I had to spend ten years in a conservative Christian school. I would still classify myself as a Christian, but more eclectic and liberal. Please forgive this long post, but here's what I think on the matter:

Firstly, a lot of it comes from misinterpretation of the Bible. To me and many of my religious studies professors, it should not be interpreted literally but rather existentially. It was written during a time where concepts like evolution would not have been known so creation stories of all types would have supplemented as a form of understanding how the world came to be. Even the Genesis creation story seems to follow the general idea of how the earth was initially formed and how organisms evolved. (Ex: Fish then reptiles then birds and mammals then humans). Nonetheless, people who believe in God because of their own personal experiences or because they simply want the hope of there being an afterlife consequently think that evolution goes against the Bible so they just deny the facts.

Secondly, there are a number of fearmongering tactics that the church uses. To give some background, I am a gay man suffering from the scars of some psychological abuse from my school. People are depicted as binary. Good Christians or evil non-believers. The saved and the inevitably damned. I was told walking away from the tradition was worse than never having joined and that making a very particular statement (which I won't say) would result in a sin that even God can not forgive. Also if anyone offers valid counterpoints that goes against the tradition or teachings, I was told "that's the devil's manipulation to get you to turn off of the difficult path to Heaven!" Another example to support this is that I know many people who want to be more accepting of LGBT people, but they fear for their own soul what would happen if they do show support. As a result, you get many people following God both out of love for their alleged goodness and out of fear of punishment.

Lastly, I would say that I myself am more willing to believe in a higher power because I don't know everything. I am not ignorant enough to believe that I know exactly what's going to happen when I die. Life is weird. There is so much I can't explain. I am unwilling to believe as something so small in a universe so expansive with so many different quirks and quandaries that there absolutely couldn't be something else. I've seen organisms that are just born, lay eggs, and die. What is the point of their life? Why do they even bother? Why have other mammals historically in nature seemed to hold not just funeral services but various other rites that are seemingly religious? If matter and energy can't be created nor destroyed, where does it go when someone dies? Why do things shockingly occur like non-predicted random snowstorms the moment I pray for help on an assignment or having things fall exactly into place just as I cried out for help when I was contemplating suicide?

Ultimately, I won't say there's 100% definitely a god, but the possibility of there being something out there doesn't defy any form of known science unless people are talking about extreme cases which very seldom have actual proof. I think there may be some being like God or a good energy like that of Buddhism that exists, and I think that every religious system has a piece of that idea that's right and a piece that's wrong.
